links.source_location: The awaiting_human stage marker is what the human_input resume payload clears

Duplication is deliberate so each architecture stays independent; cost is that the audit schema lives in three files with divergent signatures (agent_executor_version adds input_summary and actions_taken)
datetime.utcnow() is deprecated and returns a naive timestamp, wrong for an audit log; use datetime.now(timezone.utc)

make_audit mints a fresh request_id per call, so each stage of one request gets a different ID and the trail cannot be correlated; the audit requirement is structurally unmet — mint once per request and thread it through
Both are cases where a stage of the four-stage contract is nominally implemented but structurally fails its actual requirement
main.py contains scaffold text, ends with print('agent executor placeholder')

Script writes every FILES entry with mode "w"; it was run twice with different FILES contents, which is why main.py holds the scaffold text, pyproject [project] tables are duplicated and the README fence is unterminated
diagrams/*.mmd carry a stray trailing flowchart TD / sequenceDiagram line
Assert-based offline --self-check stands in for a tests/ directory because scripts/run-tests.sh requires a top-level pyproject.toml that this project lacks
Both are generator-induced defects: the scaffold emitted code whose stated run instructions do not match its import style
All three use package-relative imports, so bare `uv run main.py` raises ImportError; the fix is `uv run --project X python -m X.main` from the parent, or switching to absolute imports
Only per-version pyproject.toml files exist, so run-tests.sh skips the directory; adding a root pyproject.toml with [tool.pytest.ini_options] opts in, as projects/18-rag-citation-agent does
Per-version uv workspaces force --project selection while module execution must happen from the parent
On langchain 1.x create_agent is LangGraph underneath, so the AgentExecutor-vs-LangGraph contrast the repo exists to demonstrate no longer exists; the three variants read as a historical comparison
The missing policy tier is a gap in the approval pattern's safety guarantee
Substring matching means "I am definitely not sure" and "the Unknown Pleasures album" both trip detection — it is a grep, not a confidence estimate
With no policy tier, a confident-sounding request for a destructive action sails straight through the keyword gate
Each version carries its own audit.py copy

AgentExecutor left langchain.agents in langchain 1.0 (langchain>=0.2.0 resolves to 1.4.x, exporting only create_agent), so this version depends on langchain-classic for AgentExecutor and create_tool_calling_agent instead of pinning the whole project to a 2024-era langchain
README names resume_pipeline where CLAUDE.md names resume_with_human for the same resume hook; one of the two names is stale
